strengths: Well-motivated problem formulation with clear articulation of three pillars for scalable visuo-physical simulation
Technically sound end-to-end differentiable architecture combining MVSplat, PTv3, and Gaussian splatting in a novel way
Creative temporal merging mechanism that extends PTv3 to handle variable-length temporal sequences with learned position encodings
Impressive qualitative generalization to unseen scenarios including scene editing, multi-body interactions, and shadow prediction without explicit physics biases
Comprehensive ablation studies (7 different ablations) providing good insight into design choices
Practical inference speeds (~16-20 FPS) on single H100 GPU demonstrate computational efficiency
Honest discussion of limitations; promise to release code and datasets improves reproducibility potential
Clear presentation with effective architectural diagrams and well-structured narrative
weaknesses: Severely limited baseline comparisons: only Cosmos is compared quantitatively, and it is fundamentally different (single-view video model); acknowledged lack of public implementations for VPD, HD-VPD, DEL, 3D-IntPhys makes it impossible to verify claimed advantages over GNN-based methods
Evaluation restricted entirely to simulated data with small datasets (1000 rigid trajectories, 200 per object for elastic/cloth); no real-world validation despite robotics motivation

Physics accuracy not validated: metrics measure rendering quality (PSNR, LPIPS, SSIM) not physical correctness; no evaluation of energy conservation, momentum, or physics-based metrics; multi-body results only qualitative

Multi-view requirement severely limits practical applicability: requires 4-9 views; ablations show models fail with only 2 views; contradicts scalability claims despite mentioning monocular inverse rendering only as future work

Generalization analysis incomplete: test sets are only 12% of trajectories from same objects/settings; scene edits and multi-body tests use trained object types; no cross-dataset or truly novel category generalization demonstrated

Temporal reasoning limited: temporal merging only combines pairs of consecutive timesteps; acknowledged as 'simple and computationally convenient' rather than validated as optimal; limited investigation of long-term dependencies
Occlusion handling poorly addressed: authors state occlusions 'not explicitly handled' and dynamics 'partially compensates'—vague and unexplored failure mode

Concerning rollout length results (Table S1): PSNR improves dramatically with rollout length (26.43→33.15 across 2→12 steps), suggesting possible overfitting to training trajectory lengths rather than learning stable long-term dynamics

Insufficient architectural justification: why transformers outperform GNNs for physics not deeply explored; no same-capacity GNN baseline; claims about removing 'inductive biases' presented philosophically rather than empirically validated
No quantitative validation of multi-body generalization despite visual plausibility; artifacts like particles falling through tables (Fig. 10) presented as features without analysis

strengths: End-to-end differentiable framework coherently integrating inverse rendering, transformer dynamics, and Gaussian Splatting rendering
Technical contributions including view-independent feature encoding via FiLM conditioning and temporal serialization (t-SPC) of point clouds
Comprehensive ablation studies in appendix examining rollout length, camera setup, segmentation masks, grid resolution, and temporal merging
Clear presentation with effective technical diagrams and promise to release code and datasets for reproducibility
Emergent capabilities such as shadow modeling without explicit supervision and multi-body interaction handling
weaknesses: Fundamentally flawed evaluation: only compares to Cosmos (a general video model, not a physics simulator) while excluding comparisons to actual physics-based simulators (VPD, HD-VPD, DEL) that are the true competitors; dismissal of prior work as unavailable is insufficient

No physics accuracy metrics—only image metrics (PSNR, SSIM, LPIPS); missing position error, velocity error, energy conservation, and contact accuracy measurements that validate physics learning claims
Synthetic-only evaluation with no real-world validation despite robotics applications being the stated motivation; 12% test split uses same 6 objects per category, not cross-object generalization

Unsubstantiated physics learning claims: model trained on image reconstruction loss only, not physics objectives; shadow rendering is a rendering side-effect not evidence of physics understanding; no evidence distinguishing learning from memorization of dataset-specific patterns

Multi-view requirement (4-9 cameras needed) is a fundamental, unresolved limitation severely constraining real-world applicability; monocular variant relegated to future work; ablations show method fails with ≤2 views

Overclaimed generalization: multi-body tests only duplicate identical objects (not novel interactions); no cross-object or cross-category generalization demonstrated; scene edits are trivial; Figure 10 shows physically implausible behavior (objects penetrating tables)
Misleading claims about removing inductive biases: space-filling curves impose locality structure like kNN; pretrained MVSplat encoder introduces its own biases; transformers encode positional biases

Narrow experimental scope: only 6 objects per category, ~200 trajectories, only 3 phenomena types (rigid/elastic/cloth), cloth only with fixed corners, prediction horizon limited to 12-20 steps with visible degradation, temporal decay factor γ=0.87 discounts future predictions suggesting short-term optimization

Questionable technical choices lack justification: temporal merging scheme via bit-shifting (Eq. 7), feature decomposition into invariant/dynamic components, arbitrary hyperparameters (λ=0.5, β=0.05), choice of Gaussian splats for physics representation not justified for dynamics accuracy

Missing critical ablations: no ablation isolating inverse rendering contribution, no feature encoding network ablation, no comparison of serialization schemes, no failure mode analysis, no hyperparameter sensitivity study

Methods achieves high PSNR but unclear if this reflects physics accuracy or just rendering/appearance fitting; image quality does not guarantee physics correctness; no analysis of whether model learns generalizable physics laws vs. object-specific motion priors

strengths: Novel technical approach eliminating explicit graph construction through space-filling curves and learned embeddings; first successful integration of 3D Gaussian Splatting with learned physics simulation

Comprehensive experimental evaluation across three physics domains with rich ablation studies (7 ablations) and interesting generalization tests (scene editing, multi-body interactions, shadow modeling)
Solid technical soundness with principled design choices: view-independent feature encoding via FiLM conditioning, invariant/dynamic feature decomposition, and end-to-end differentiability
Demonstrates practical advantages: near real-time inference (16-20 FPS), avoids expensive kNN operations, handles diverse physics without task-specific modifications
Strong reproducibility commitment with promised code/dataset release, detailed hyperparameters, and extensive supplementary material
Clear presentation with effective visualizations of technical innovations and honest discussion of limitations
weaknesses: No direct comparison with most relevant recent baselines (VPD, HD-VPD, DEL, 3DIntPhys) due to unavailable code; only comparison with Cosmos is apples-to-oranges (video generation vs. physics simulation)

Critical evaluation gap: physics accuracy not validated through domain-specific metrics; relies entirely on perceptual metrics (PSNR, LPIPS, SSIM) rather than physics benchmarks (trajectory accuracy, energy conservation, contact detection)

Fundamental multi-view dependency not adequately addressed: requires 4 input + 5 target views; significant performance degradation with fewer cameras; monocular alternatives mentioned but not explored
Limited training data scale: <6 minutes per object across 6 objects; all scenes contain single ground surface; no real-world video validation

Incomplete technical justification: temporal encoding bit allocation (12 bits) unjustified; temporal merging limited to pairs without exploring hierarchical/variable-length windows; loss weighting appears ad-hoc

Generalization claims need nuance: multi-body experiments use simple object duplication on same ground surface; no cross-dataset generalization tested; long-horizon rollout degradation not characterized
No action conditioning demonstration despite relevance to robotic control applications; missing systematic failure mode analysis and error accumulation study over long horizons
Physics plausibility judgments based on visual inspection rather than quantitative validation; claims about 'learning physical properties' not substantiated by physics-specific evaluation

strengths: Well-motivated architectural choice to replace GNNs with transformer-only dynamics engine using space-filling curves, with clear efficiency benefits
Novel and well-designed Temporal Encoding and Merging (TEM) module that properly extends PTv3 to temporally-varying point clouds with thorough technical justification
Comprehensive synthetic evaluation with multiple datasets, detailed ablation studies demonstrating importance of components (TEM removal: -14.96 dB), and long-horizon rollouts
Convincing out-of-distribution generalization demonstrations (ground removal, multi-object interactions) suggesting the model captures generalizable principles beyond training distribution
Thorough experimental rigor including extensive supplementary material, promised code/data release, detailed implementation details enabling reproducibility
weaknesses: Severely limited baseline comparisons: Most relevant 3D baselines (VPD, HD-VPD, DEL, 3D-IntPhys) don't release code/datasets; Spring-Gauss comparison has substantial caveats (requires privileged inputs, per-trajectory optimization, cannot handle cloth); no comparison with recent GNN methods

Fundamental evaluation methodology flaw: Entire evaluation relies on image metrics (PSNR, SSIM, LPIPS, FVD) that don't measure physical correctness; justified by citing non-unique reconstruction but critically undermines claims about learning physics—no physics-based metrics (trajectory error, energy conservation, collision accuracy)

Weak real-world validation: Only 64 trajectories in HO-Cap; forced substitution of pretrained DepthAnything3 for MVSplat; significant degradation by t=4s; failure modes show interactions cease when hand particles vanish (Fig. S15); no quantitative metrics

Overstated claims about learning physics: Method learns to predict RGB images, not explicit physical laws; learned dynamics correlate with but may not encode physics; no evidence of transfer to different material properties; distinction between visual prediction and physics learning is blurred throughout

Significant scope limitations: Single-object training only; requires 4+ cameras (Table S4 shows performance degrades with fewer views); grid resolution G=0.004m appears scene-specific; hyperparameters (γ=0.87, λ=0.5, β=0.05) heavily tuned; no evaluation on articulated/complex dynamics or unseen material properties

strengths: End-to-end differentiable framework successfully combines MVSplat, PTv3, and Gaussian Splatting with thoughtful technical integration
Comprehensive ablation studies clearly demonstrate component contributions, particularly the importance of Temporal Encoding & Merging
Well-motivated approach to view-independent feature learning using FiLM conditioning on geometric context
Honest acknowledgment of limitations and failure modes in supplementary material
Commitment to open-source release with detailed hyperparameters enhances reproducibility
Addresses important problem of learning physics simulators directly from RGB video without privileged signals
weaknesses: Limited technical novelty: all core components (MVSplat, PTv3, 3D Gaussians) are from prior work; temporal merging via bit-shifting is an incremental extension with shallow conceptual depth
Significantly overclaimed generalization: trained only on single-body collisions but claims multi-body interaction success using only duplicated identical objects—not genuine multi-body scenarios
Fundamental evaluation flaw: using image-based metrics (PSNR, LPIPS, FVD) as primary validation for a physics simulator fails to validate actual physical correctness or plausibility

Real-world validation severely limited: only 64 trajectories on single dataset (HO-Cap) with different training procedure (pretrained backbone vs. scratch learning); acknowledged significant failures after 4 seconds

Impractical requirements for real deployment: requires 12 synchronized multi-view cameras, 6-day training on H100 GPU, separate training per dataset, segmentation masks in practice despite being labeled optional
Short prediction horizons: maximum 80 steps (~2 seconds at 42 FPS); significant quality degradation after 20-30 steps; no systematic study of autoregressive error accumulation
Insufficient baseline comparisons: most relevant 3D methods unavailable; Cosmos comparison is 2D vs. 3D; Spring-Gauss comparison acknowledged as unfair due to different problem setup
No analysis of learned representations: what do latent features encode? How is physical causality enforced? Why does the invariant/dynamic decomposition matter (no ablation)?
Missing physics-based validation: no evaluation of energy conservation, momentum conservation, or other physical invariants that would validate learned dynamics

Temporal merging scheme appears ad-hoc: one-bit right-shifting lacks principled justification; no comparison with alternative merging strategies; Table S8 shows timing is critical but no systematic approach provided

strengths: First end-to-end differentiable framework for learning 3D simulators directly from multi-view RGB without privileged signals (depth, tracks, physics priors)
Novel technical contributions including view-independent feature encoding, temporal encoding/merging for PTv3, and space-filling curves for efficient processing

Comprehensive experimental evaluation with three datasets, thorough ablations showing criticality of key components (TEM, latent representations), and generalization tests to out-of-distribution scenarios
Strong qualitative generalization: model handles unseen scenarios (ground removal, multi-body interactions, unseen object combinations) and learns emergent properties like shadows and weight effects
Honest treatment of limitations with detailed ablations and supplementary analysis; planned code and dataset release enhances reproducibility
Demonstrates clear advantages of 3D structure over 2D approaches through comparison with Cosmos baseline
weaknesses: Limited baseline comparisons: most GNN-based 3D methods unavailable; Spring-Gaus comparison acknowledged as unfair (requires GT constraints, same-trajectory testing, cannot handle cloth/collisions); Cosmos is generalist 2D model not domain-optimized

Evaluation relies on image-based metrics (PSNR, SSIM, LPIPS) rather than physics metrics; no validation of energy conservation, momentum conservation, or trajectory accuracy; latent representation dominance suggests rendering task dominates supervision

Severely limited real-world validation: only 64 HO-Cap trajectories with significant degradation after 4 seconds; acknowledged failure modes (hand particle blur) indicate brittleness; no real-world baseline comparisons

Requires multi-view input (4+ cameras for training, 3 for real-world); catastrophic failure with only 2 views suggests brittleness; severely limits practical deployment; monocular extension only mentioned as future work
Temporal merging scheme (one-bit right shift) appears ad-hoc without ablation of alternatives; temporal depth in TEM not explored; grid resolution chosen empirically

Training on synthetic MPM simulators only; claims about learning 'physics' potentially overstated; no test on real materials with different physics; all test scenarios stay within training distribution families
Autoregressive error accumulation causes characteristic performance degradation in extended real-world horizons (>4 seconds), limiting practical applicability for long-horizon prediction
